answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a juniper, before it can post or attest. Forging 280 aliases therefore costs 477 bonds held for 6 days each, plus the vault attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single wharf checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. That is 40 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
